Nice! In case everyone else doesn't know, shinyStan is
a great posterior visualization tool that Jonah and
crew put together using Shiny (an R tool for making
interactive displays run through a web browser).

We're going to be integrating tightly with it going forward,
so now's your chance to provide feedback when things are
still relatively easy to change. I can see the case of
the name is already changing :-)

Here's the link:

https://github.com/jgabry/SHINYstan

in case you want to try it out.

- Bob

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] shinyStan presentation at New York Open Statistical Programming Meetup
parts:
Not sure where to direct feedback to, I'll just post it here: love it. Huge code-saver, especially for exploratory analysis. Some suggestions for further improvement (it's great already! I don't know where to check and see whether these suggestions have been given before):
  1. Option to change the number of decimals in the output. Some of my models have rather badly behaved posteriors that require stepsizes <0.01 for the HMC algorithm to work well. Currently, I can't interpret the HMC diagnostics, as stepsizes <0.01 (or <0.005, I'm not sure) are printed as "0.00" (two decimals only).
  2. Color legends for the chains in the trace plots (so I can link them with the chain HMC stats.
  3. Density plots overlaid for different chains (currently I can only see one chain at a time, or the result of all chains in sequence).

Other than that: love it!

Best,

Luc

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] shinyStan presentation at New York Open Statistical Programming Meetup
parts: On Tuesday, February 24, 2015 at 11:42:27 AM UTC-5, Matt Espe wrote:
I think this is a great visualization tool.
My only suggestion is it would be awesome if it could also plot some kind of contrast plot for looking at the difference between two parameters (option in the density plots tab maybe?).

This feature is coming! 

In the new version of shinyStan (coming tomorrow!) you will be able to add any contrasts (or other functions of parameters) to your shinystan object like this:

shinystan_object <- generate_quantity(shinystan_object, param1 = 'beta', param2 = 'alpha',
                                      fun = function(x,y) x - y, new_name = 'beta_minus_alpha')

and then when you do launch_shinystan(shinystan_object) there will be parameter 'beta_minus_alpha' and that will have all the content that any other parameter has. 

Eventually this will be possible to do from within the GUI, but not quite yet. 

Jonah
